description: Exhaustive enumeration of ALL 2D and 3D milling operations with every parameter, dialog, physics link, and tribal knowledge

tool_settings.name: Tool Settings
tool_settings.description: Common tool definition parameters shared across operations

operations_2d.name: Face Milling
operations_2d.description: Planar face milling for top surface finishing and roughing

tribal_tips.text: Use 1.3x part width for full coverage in single pass
For aluminum, increase RPM 2-3x over steel, reduce feed per tooth by 20%
High-feed face mills: ap < 1mm but stepover up to 90%

operations_2d.name: Pocket Milling (Standard)
operations_2d.description: Closed pocket roughing and finishing with multiple strategy options

tribal_tips.text: For D2 steel pockets, use trochoidal with 10% stepover max
Helix entry: diameter at least 2x tool diameter for stability
Leave 0.15mm on walls for finish pass to remove deflection marks

operations_2d.name: Pocket Milling (Open)
operations_2d.description: Open pocket machining with entry from outside boundary

tribal_tips.text: Open pockets: enter tangent from open side, avoid ramping

operations_2d.name: Pocket Milling (Island)
operations_2d.description: Pocket with internal islands/bosses to avoid

tribal_tips.text: For thin-wall islands, finish walls before floor to prevent deflection

operations_2d.name: Contour Milling
operations_2d.description: 2D profile/contour machining along walls and edges

tribal_tips.text: For tight tolerances, run 2 finish passes: first removes deflection, second hits size
Climb milling for finish, conventional for roughing in hardened steel

operations_2d.name: Slot Milling
operations_2d.description: Slot machining for grooves, channels, and keyways

tribal_tips.text: Full-width slot: reduce feed 50%, depth per pass 30%
For keyways, use dedicated slot drills with center-cutting capability
Through-coolant essential for deep slots in stainless

operations_2d.name: T-Slot Milling
operations_2d.description: T-slot machining for clamping grooves and T-nuts

tribal_tips.text: Always machine slot first, then undercut. Reverse causes chatter.
T-slot cutters: max 0.5mm depth per pass in steel
Use arbor support for long T-slots to prevent cutter deflection

operations_2d.name: Thread Milling
operations_2d.description: Helical interpolation thread milling for internal and external threads

tribal_tips.text: Thread mill: climb for right-hand threads, conventional for left-hand
Single-point thread mills for large diameters, multi-tooth for small bores
Leave 0.05mm extra on major diameter for plating/coating allowance
Pre-drill 0.5mm deeper than thread depth for chip clearance

operations_2d.name: Chamfer Milling
operations_2d.description: Edge chamfering and deburring along 2D contours

tribal_tips.text: Use ball endmill for variable-depth chamfers on 3D edges
Tip offset 0.1mm prevents digging at corners

operations_2d.name: Plunge Roughing
operations_2d.description: Z-axis plunge milling for roughing deep cavities and hard materials

tribal_tips.text: Plunge milling ideal for deep cavities in hardened steel (45+ HRC)
70% stepover optimal for insert overlap without missing material
Always follow with contour cleanup - plunge leaves scallops

operations_2d.name: Rest Machining
operations_2d.description: Clear remaining material from previous operations using reference toolpath

tribal_tips.text: Rest tool should be max 50% of previous tool diameter
Add 0.5mm extension to catch deflection from previous op

operations_2d.name: Deburring
operations_2d.description: Automated deburring along edges with force or depth control

tribal_tips.text: For consistent deburr depth, use ball endmill at 45-degree lean
Reduce feed 50% at sharp corners to prevent gouging

operations_3d.name: Shape Offset Roughing (Optimised Roughing)
operations_3d.description: High-efficiency roughing with offset patterns following 3D surface shape

tribal_tips.text: HPC roughing: full flute depth with 10-15% stepover beats shallow wide cuts
For hardened steel, use adaptive with max 60-degree engagement
Trochoidal corners prevent tool shock and extend life 2-3x

operations_3d.name: Z-Level Finishing
operations_3d.description: Constant-Z waterline finishing for steep walls and vertical faces

tribal_tips.text: For Ra 0.8, use scallop height 0.005mm max
Climb on downcut, conventional on upcut for consistent finish
Ball endmill: stepdown = 0.1 * diameter for good cusp balance

operations_3d.name: Equidistant Finishing
operations_3d.description: Constant scallop height finishing with variable stepover following surface curvature

tribal_tips.text: Constant scallop = uniform finish quality regardless of surface angle
Set min stepover to 0.1*D to prevent excessive toolpath density

operations_3d.name: Profile Finishing (3D Contour)
operations_3d.description: Follow 3D surface profiles with controlled contact point

tribal_tips.text: Flowline patterns follow natural surface curvature - best for organic shapes
Add 5-10 degree lead angle to prevent rubbing at tool center

operations_3d.name: Pencil Tracing
operations_3d.description: Trace internal corners and fillets with small tool for corner cleanup

tribal_tips.text: Tool radius should match or be slightly smaller than fillet radius
Multiple pencil passes remove deflection marks from previous roughing
Lollipop cutters reach undercut fillets that ball mills cannot

operations_3d.name: 3D Rest Machining
operations_3d.description: Machine remaining material from previous 3D operations

tribal_tips.text: Rest tool = 50% of previous tool for good corner access
Extend boundary 1mm to catch deflection artifacts from roughing

operations_3d.name: Horizontal Area Machining
operations_3d.description: Machine flat/horizontal areas of 3D surfaces with optimized 2D-like patterns

tribal_tips.text: Use flat endmill for true horizontal surfaces - ball leaves scallops
Overlap 1mm with Z-level pass to blend transition zones

operations_3d.name: Plane Machining
operations_3d.description: Machine planar faces within 3D models with face mill efficiency

tribal_tips.text: Plane machining with face mill = 3-5x faster than ball endmill on flats
66% stepover balances MRR with insert life

operations_3d.name: Arbitrary Stock Roughing
operations_3d.description: Machine non-prismatic stock shapes (castings, forgings, pre-machined)

tribal_tips.text: Scan stock with CMM or laser for accurate arbitrary stock model
Air-cut avoidance saves 20-40% cycle time on near-net shapes

operations_3d.name: ISO Machining (Isoparametric)
operations_3d.description: Follow surface UV directions for consistent toolpath on NURBS surfaces

tribal_tips.text: ISO machining follows natural surface flow - ideal for automotive body panels
Check UV direction on CAD model - some surfaces have twisted UVs

operations_3d.name: Radial Machining
operations_3d.description: Radial/spoke pattern machining for round features and bosses

tribal_tips.text: Radial patterns ideal for hub/boss features - hides tool marks in spoke lines
For turbine blades, combine radial with flowline for optimal finish
